name: org.machanism.machai:gw-maven-plugin
description: GW Maven Plugin is a Java 8 Maven plugin that connects Maven projects to the Machai Ghostwriter AI-assisted guided file-processing workflow. It scans selected project content for embedded guidance comments or executes a named act or direct prompt. The plugin supplies four Maven goals for project-wide and reactor-module workflows: gw:gw, gw:act, gw:gw-per-module, and gw:act-per-module. It resolves Maven project, module, settings, dependency, and parallel-build context; accepts paths, exclusions, additional instructions, provider/model settings, acts, and configuration inputs; and can obtain provider credentials from Maven settings. It also exposes Java class discovery and reflection tools that locate classes by simple-name regular expression and return declared member, annotation, source, classpath, and Maven-artifact metadata. It is intended for documentation maintenance, source and configuration analysis, repeatable guided transformations, and Maven-integrated AI automation.

constructors.description: Creates class-discovery tools and registers the supplied Maven project. The project compile classpath and output directories are used for subsequent class lookup and reflective inspection.

examples.description: Create the integration with the current MavenProject before requesting class discovery or class metadata. The obtainMavenProject helper represents Maven-plugin context supplied by the caller.

constructors.description: Creates an empty class-tool registry. Register each Maven project with scanProjectClasses before calling findClass or getClassInfo.

examples.description: Use the empty constructor when one tool instance must serve several Maven projects, then register the active project explicitly.

constructors.description: Creates metadata storage for one Maven project. The holder builds a project-aware URL class loader and resolves visible classes, source files, output paths, and dependency artifact coordinates.

examples.description: Create a holder for a Maven project and load a known fully qualified application class from its configured classpath.

features.name: gw:gw
features.description: Runs the aggregator guidance workflow. It creates a Ghostwriter GuidanceProcessor, derives effective Maven and provider configuration, scans the selected project content for guidance comments, and supports project-wide, multi-module, and parallel execution.

examples.description: Step 1: add the plugin to the Maven build. Step 2: configure a provider/model and the source path or instruction file. Step 3: run gw:gw from the project root to process guidance-bearing Java files while skipping build output.

features.name: gw:act
features.description: Runs an explicit Ghostwriter act or prompt. The aggregator act workflow supports selected files or paths, named act definitions, instructions, exclusions, Maven settings credentials, and reverse module ordering with submodules processed before parents.

examples.snippet:
mvn org.machanism.machai:gw-maven-plugin:1.4.2:act -Dgw.act=review
mvn gw:act -Dgw.act='>Update public API documentation' -Dgw.path=src/main/java
mvn gw:act -Dgw.acts=.ghostwriter/acts -Dgw.act=review
examples.description: Step 1: invoke the installed plugin by coordinates, or configure it in the build for the short goal form. Step 2: provide a named act, or prefix a prompt-only act with >. Step 3: optionally point gw.acts at local act definitions and restrict processing with gw.path.

features.name: find_class
features.description: Finds fully qualified Java class names whose simple names completely match a regular expression. The lookup uses the registered Maven project's compile classpath and output directories and rejects result sets larger than ten entries.

examples.description: After registering the Maven project, search for service classes without knowing their packages. Pass an exact returned fully qualified name to getClassInfo.

features.name: get_class_info
features.signature: public java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.lang.Object> org.machanism.machai.gw.maven.tools.ClassFunctionalTools.getClassInfo(java.lang.String className, java.io.File projectDir) throws java.lang.ClassNotFoundException
features.description: Loads a fully qualified class through the registered project's class loader and returns structured metadata for modifiers, direct superclass and interfaces, declared non-private fields and methods, constructors, annotations, source path, classpath location, and dependency artifact.

examples.snippet:
java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.lang.Object> info = tools.getClassInfo("com.example.orders.OrderService", project.getBasedir());
java.lang.Object methods = info.get("methods");
examples.description: Inspect a discovered application class and use the methods property to document or analyze its declared accessible API.

features.name: scanProjectClasses
features.description: Registers or refreshes class metadata for a Maven project base directory. Re-register a project after source, dependency, or build-output changes because discovery metadata is cached.

examples.description: Refresh class metadata after a build, then search the refreshed project registry for an exact controller simple name.

examples.title: Install, configure, and run guidance processing
steps: Add org.machanism.machai:gw-maven-plugin:1.4.2 to the build plugins section of pom.xml.
Configure the AI provider/model and, if needed, configure a Maven settings.xml server referenced by genai.serverId so credentials remain outside the project POM.
Place guidance comments in project files and run mvn gw:gw with gw.path and gw.excludes appropriate to the target content.
Review the generated changes, then run the normal Maven test lifecycle.

examples.title: Run a focused documentation act
steps: Configure the plugin and provider credentials as for guidance processing.
Choose a predefined act name or supply a direct prompt prefixed with >.
Run gw:act against the API source directory and inspect the resulting documentation changes.
Use Maven parallel execution only when project workflow and provider capacity permit it.
